questions.prompt: How do you set a fixed title and description for a page?

options.text: Export a metadata object from the page or layout (a Server Component)
Write <title> and <meta> tags in a <head> you render yourself
Return them from a Client Component

questions.explanation: Export a metadata object (typed Metadata) from a Server Component page/layout; Next.js renders the correct head tags.

questions.prompt: When should you use generateMetadata instead of the metadata object?

options.text: When the metadata depends on data, like a post's title
Whenever the page is a Client Component

questions.explanation: generateMetadata is an async function for data-driven metadata; in Next.js 15 its params is a Promise you await.

questions.prompt: In a root layout, title: { template: '%s | My Site' } applies a suffix. What placeholder represents the child page's title? Type it.
questions.explanation: %s is replaced by the child page's title, producing e.g. 'Pricing | My Site'.

questions.prompt: Which statements about the Metadata API are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: It only works in Server Components
openGraph fields control social link previews
Files like favicon.ico and sitemap.xml are recognized automatically
You must hand-write all <head> tags yourself

questions.explanation: Metadata works in Server Components, openGraph drives previews, and file conventions are auto-detected — so you don't hand-write head tags.

questions.prompt: Match each metadata tool to its purpose.
questions.explanation: Static values use the metadata object, dynamic ones use generateMetadata, templates unify titles, and openGraph controls previews.

questions.prompt: Order how a blog post's <title> is produced with a layout template.

items.text: The root layout defines title.template '%s | DevBlog'
generateMetadata awaits params and fetches the post
Next.js renders '<post title> | DevBlog' in the head

questions.explanation: The layout template sets the pattern; generateMetadata supplies the page title, which the template wraps into the final head title.
